messages.text:
Although your initial estimate was 110 000 particles, I would like you to make 10k with E\~10 to 80 GeV flat in phi from eta -3 to 3, and then show make a sigma(E)/E plot vs |eta| in 10 bins and in the folded phi in 10 bins.\
The local CPU has 24 core, use multithreading with 12.

Check if we have enough disk space for this, if not trimm down to fit.

I’ll prepare the 10,000-electron sample with 12 threads and check disk space before running it. I’ll use uniform energy from 10–80 GeV, uniform η from −3 to 3, and uniform φ. I’ll also check the ECAL symmetry and response definition so the folded-φ and σ(E)/E plots are well defined.

There is about **408 GiB free**, so disk space should accommodate the full 10,000 events. I’ll retain a safety margin and check the projection after a pilot batch.

I’m using the ACTS Spack and repository validation workflows. The Spack fingerprints have changed, so I’ll reverify the runtime. I’ll also get an independent physics review of the resolution estimator: with a 10–80 GeV spectrum, the raw energy spread would mostly measure the beam’s energy range.

Completed **all 10,000 electrons with 12 threads**, with no trimming: uniform E = 10–80 GeV, η = −3 to 3, and full φ.

**9 min 46 s · 2.37 GiB peak RAM · 12.60 GB output · 401 GiB still free.** All events passed readback.

![Angular response plots]([redacted]

Each projection has **10 bins**, with 95% bootstrap intervals. These show **raw visible-response widths**, including geometric losses. Seam-adjacent φ bins reach about **110%**, versus **23–25%** inside.
